description: An oscillator locked to an incoming clock, its frequency set as a ratio of that clock chosen from a grid of scales, with a morphing wavetable for its shape

params.text: Picks the X coordinate in the ratio grid, which is the numerator of the frequency ratio in most groups and a scan through an arpeggio in the Arppegios group
Picks the Y coordinate in the ratio grid, which is the denominator of the frequency ratio in most groups and the chord or quantization in the others
Scans across the current wavetable, morphing the shape of the oscillator
Sets one of the two voltages the main output runs between, -5V to +5V; patching the A input takes this knob out of circuit
Multiplies the B input by -1 to +1 to set the other voltage the main output runs between; with nothing patched to B the input reads 5V, so the knob alone gives -5V to +5V
Attenuates the assignable modulation input before the module adds it, from nothing at fully counter-clockwise to all of it at fully clockwise
Attenuates the Wave shape CV input before the module adds it, from nothing at fully counter-clockwise to all of it at fully clockwise
Steps through what happens to the A and B levels at each cycle: Off, Track and Hold, or Resample
Steps through the four scales of the current group, wrapping round at the end
Steps through what the assignable modulation input reaches: Y Ratio, Phase or Skew
Steps through how quickly the oscillator chases a new ratio: Slow, Medium, Fast or Instantaneous
Steps through the group of scales and waves the module works from: Harmonics, Arppegios, 1V/Oct or Rhythms
Steps through the four wavetables of the current group, wrapping round at the end
Tapping this sets the tempo the oscillator locks to, in place of a pulse at the Sync input

inputs.text: One of the two voltages the main output runs between; patched here, it overrides the manual A input knob
The other voltage the main output runs between, multiplied by the B knob; unpatched it reads 5V
Moves the X coordinate through the ratio grid, at 384 units of the internal 12-bit control range per volt
Reaches whichever of Y Ratio, Phase or Skew the MOD CV destination button has chosen, through the MOD CV amount knob
Scans the wavetable, through the Wave shape CV amount knob
The clock the oscillator locks to; each rising edge is measured to work out the tempo
A rising edge here restarts the oscillator's phase without changing the tempo it has measured

outputs.text: The oscillator, scaled between the A and B levels
A 5V gate, high during the attack or a delta pulse according to the Logic Out menu setting
The oscillator itself as a voltage, without the A and B scaling
A 5V gate that fires when the frequency ratio changes

notes: the A input is normalled to the A knob: with nothing patched the knob sets that voltage, and patching a cable into A takes the knob out of circuit entirely.
the B input is normalled to 5V and the B knob multiplies whatever arrives by -1 to +1. Unpatched the knob is a -5V to +5V source; patched it attenuverts the cable.
the main output is the module's own signal scaled between the A and B levels. Set both of those to 0V and the main output is silent whatever else the module is doing.
each of the six buttons steps to the next mode when clicked. Hovering one names the mode and its number; right-click and you can type either to jump straight to it.
menu: High during attack — makes the gate output high while the wave is rising; found under the Logic Out heading
Delta — makes the gate output a pulse at each change rather than a gate; found under the Logic Out heading
Triangle — sends a plain triangle to the contour output; found under the Signal Out heading
Contour — sends the shaped wave to the contour output; found under the Signal Out heading
Quadrature: 0 degrees, 90 degrees, 180 degrees, 270 degrees — shifts the contour output's phase against the main output
Group waves — restricts the wavetable button to the four waves belonging to the current group; found under the Wave Options heading
Global waves — lets the wavetable button reach every wave in the loaded set; found under the Wave Options heading
Stock presets: Harmonic Osc, Arpeggiated Osc, Bohlen-Pierce Modes, Modal Quantizer, Sequence, Tempo-Synced LFO — sets all six buttons at once to a factory combination
Select wavetable set — loads a wavetable file from disk in place of the one the module ships with
